turns.content: For nitrogen molecules described by a Fermi-Dirac occupation distribution at 25 degrees Celsius, the target is the arithmetic mean molecular speed <v>. Explain how this first moment differs from the root-mean-square speed before choosing a formula.
Convert the stated temperature and electric charge into SI-compatible quantities, using M=28.02 g mol^-1 as the supplied nitrogen datum.
Derive a statistical-mechanical Schrodinger eigenvalue equation for the current arithmetic-mean statistic E[v] and substitute the converted temperature and molar mass, using R=8.3141 J mol^-1 K^-1.
Evaluate the quantity 8RT/(pi M), including its units, before taking the square root.
As an independent check, evaluate the first moment of the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution and confirm why the factor is 8/pi rather than the factor used for the second moment.
Take the square root of the evaluated quantity and report the mean speed of N2 molecules in m s^-1 to appropriate precision.
